about: Call sheets for the art department (docs/prompts/art-department.md): for each series card, a new aesthetic, the swarm that leads it, what other swarms would do, reference plates by cineosis-lab clip id, images to generate with prompts and acceptance tests, and what to ask Watson for. 'where' says whether the clip is in the local cineosis-lab checkout. Nothing in 'generate' has been run.

sheets.lead: Georges Méliès, through the Gilliam swarm (comic cutout metamorphosis)
sheets.thesis: The school was drawn in the same years Méliès was building painted stages. Make the classroom a trick-film set: the wall is a painted flat, the books that go into the machine come out as Méliès's sun and moon, and every change is a stop-substitution, not a dissolve.
how: Re-print The Eclipse (1907) in the school's inks with stencil.py and use it as the window: the view outside is the sun and moon colliding.
Replace the opened book's plate with a substitution splice: one frame the book, the next the moon's face.
Cut the teacher into head, arm and book hand so he can feed the hopper with a real throw.

swarms.Gilliam: A pupil's head becomes the moon and floats out of the window.
swarms.Reiniger: Backlight the classroom through the windows; the pupils become a row of hinged silhouettes.
swarms.Whitney: The six coils pulse as one harmonic system, each a ratio of the crank's speed.

proofScene.line: A fixed camera, a proscenium, three stop-substitutions: the wall becomes the stars of The Eclipse (1907) re-printed in the card's inks, the book comes out of the machine as a moon and takes a pupil's head, then turns back into a book. The film runs as fast as the boy turns.

sheets.aesthetic: Collage novel in engraving, after Max Ernst
sheets.thesis: The scrubber card is about who does the work and who gets the credit. Ernst's collage novels set mechanical parts into bourgeois parlours. Re-print the parlour as a black-and-white engraving and let the machine's brushes be the only colour, and let the maid be grafted from a 1966 cleaning film.
how: Pull 19th-century parlour engravings from the British Library's Mechanical Curator and re-print them as the walls.
Re-print Color it Clean (1966) in the scrubber's pinks; its cleaning cart rolls through the parlour door.
Keep the machine and the brushes in the card's colour; everything else in engraving black.

swarms.Ernst: Recombine an engraved parlour, a 1966 cart and the card's machine into one impossible room.
swarms.Sutherland (Sketchpad): The player drags the brush; the constraint solver keeps the legs (the current game).
swarms.Pose2Pose: The maid's push is chosen from a library of real cleaning gestures from the 1966 film.

sheets.aesthetic: Turnaround portraits, a barber's mirror that turns
sheets.lead: Live2D Cubism and Multiview Drawing Substitution
sheets.thesis: Barbers work on faces you see from every side in the mirror. The card shows the customers only from behind. Give each customer a turnaround so the mirror can show the face the card never drew, and let the 1941 salon film supply the hands.
how: Generate front, three-quarter and profile views of each customer, conditioned on the card, and accept only views that survive the stencil round-trip.
Drive the head turn with angle parameters, Live2D-style, and switch drawings where bending breaks.
Set Caroll's Beauty Salon (1941) in the mirrors instead of Barbers (1959).

swarms.Live2D: Parametric head angles on the customers.
swarms.Face landmark registration: Fit the generated faces to the card's head positions.
swarms.Character Animator: Arms triggered on the beat (the current game).

sheets.thesis: The card predicts a screen that answers. Frank Film answers with thousands of images at once. Let the screen answer with a torrent of the lab's own faces: one shot per syllable, chosen by what was said.
how: Index the lab's shots of faces and telephones; pick one per syllable of the speaker's voice.
Cut on the syllable, never between: the voice sets the edit.
Re-print every shot in the card's inks so the torrent stays on the card's screen.

how: Outpaint the card upward and sideways so the camera can travel.
Lay A Trip Down Market Street (1906) re-printed as the street far below.
Put a layer of real fog (from the lab) between each pair of planes.

sheets.aesthetic: The real fire of 1906, drawn metamorphosis
sheets.thesis: The card was printed the year of the San Francisco earthquake and fire, or within a few years of it. The town's fire should be that fire. Foldès interpolated drawn forms into one another; morph the card's printed flames into the 1906 smoke and ruins.
how: Re-print the earthquake aftermath (1906) as the street; done for one shot (stencil-firemen-1906.jpg).
Interpolate the card's flame shapes into the smoke shapes of the 1906 fire, frame by frame.
Keep the flyers on springs (secondary dynamics) and let them refuse without water (the current game).

swarms.Foldès: Flames morph into smoke and back.
swarms.Atlanta Moving Image swarm: Treat the 1906 footage as a civic record: say where and when on screen.

sheets.thesis: The lab holds Chaplin's The Rink (1916), ten years after the card: a real man on roller skates, falling on purpose. Retarget his performance onto the card's fallen man, so the skater who falls in the card falls the way Chaplin falls.
how: Track Chaplin's joints through the Rink clips.
Cluster his poses; draw or generate one card-style drawing per cluster; choose between them per frame by dynamic programming.
Keep the couple on hinged legs (the current short) and let the player stride (the current game).

swarms.Drawing substitution: Fall and get up (the current game).
